name: Carr's Table Water
desc: Crisp, plain and thin as a roof slate, baked in Carlisle since the 1850s. Meant for cheese, eaten with anything. Restores 55 HP.

name: Rum Nicky
desc: A Cumbrian tart of dates, ginger, butter and a good glug of rum, in a shortcrust case. Born of the old port trade at Whitehaven. Restores 130 HP.

name: Cumberland Sausage
desc: Coiled in a ring and sold by the length, peppery and coarse, with a protected name. Don't cut it into links. Restores 180 HP.

name: Selkirk Bannock
desc: A rich, buttery fruit bread, first sold in Selkirk in the 1800s, and said to be a favourite of Queen Victoria. Restores 120 HP.

name: Border Tart
desc: Sweet pastry packed with raisins, nuts and cherry, which has stopped many a hill walker dead in the doorway. Restores 150 HP.

name: Tweed Swatch
desc: A swatch of Border tweed, rough, thick and made to turn a shower. Its name, they say, began as a clerk's misspelling of 'tweel'. The weavers are too polite to say so.

name: Cornet's Colours
desc: The town's silk standard, folded in a tea-towel. Carry it across the marches, and for goodness' sake don't let a rival rider near it.

name: Reiver's Bonnet
desc: A steel cap dented at every border since the 1500s. The wearer always seems to be out after dark.
msg: {name}'s Reiver's Bonnet gleamed in the dark!

name: Cornet's Sash
desc: Red, white and blue silk, worn across the chest by the rider who carries the town's colours. It makes the wearer sit a little straighter.
effect_text: Speed up when it first comes out.
msg: {name}'s Cornet's Sash made it feel ready to ride!

name: Heart of the Bruce
desc: A little silver pin in the shape of a crowned heart, like the one on the stone at Melrose. Brave deeds are said to follow it.
msg: {name}'s Heart of the Bruce took the sting out of it!
